scope: S2 .github/workflows/arch-snapshot.yml (lane-found, same pattern; folded in with human approval)

before.harness-security.yml: top-level contents: write; one job `security` runs npx harness validate/check-deps/check-security, then pushes chore/security-ledger
before.arch-snapshot.yml: top-level contents: write; one job `snapshot` runs npx harness snapshot capture, then pushes chore/arch-timeline

after.harness-security.yml: top-level contents: read; `security` (required, read) uploads the ledger files on push to main; `ledger` (needs security, push-to-main only, contents: write, concurrency ledger-chore/security-ledger) downloads under runner.temp, copies the two files, pushes; no npx
after.arch-snapshot.yml: top-level contents: read; `snapshot` (read) uploads the timeline; `push` (needs snapshot, contents: write) downloads under runner.temp, copies the timeline, pushes; no npx

failedBeforeFix: workflow-hygiene: 'runs npx in no job that holds contents: write' received ['security'] / ['snapshot']; 'grants top-level contents: write only to allowlisted workflows' received ['arch-snapshot.yml','harness-security.yml']. 25 of 40 new tests red on 871649d5.
assumptions: The `ledger` job is advisory, not required: it is skipped on every PR, so requiring it would block every PR on a skipped job.
upload-artifact@v7 stores the files relative to their common ancestor (the workspace root), so the download holds `.harness/...` and `docs/...` at those relative paths.
download-artifact@v8 is used because the repo uses no download-artifact yet and v8 is current; its digest-mismatch default is `error`.
Read-only scan jobs keep the default persist-credentials: a read token on a public repo grants nothing the public does not already have.
release.yml and wiki-sync.yml keep their top-level write and are allowlisted with reasons; narrowing them is out of scope.
refresh-arch-baseline.yml runs the harness CLI in a job with job-level contents: write + pull-requests: write. Same class, not named by #1426, reported rather than fixed.
